\chapter{The correspondence with the C code}\label{chap:correspondence}

The model is checked against ratpoints v3.1.1 (commit \texttt{1a998538dfa8}). The C files below are those of the library and \texttt{main.c}, whose parts that the command-line program does not mirror are to be excluded. Every line of code of them lies in at most one recorded range: a range is either modelled by the Lean declarations named, or excluded from the model with a reason. Each recorded range is checked against the text it had when it was reviewed.

\item \csource{find_points.c}{1619}{1623}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{1639}{1650}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett}: natural numbers for the \texttt{unsigned long}s, the product \texttt{u m} exact as the 128-bit product of the C code, and the difference exact, which does not wrap since the quotient times \texttt{p} is at most \texttt{u} for \texttt{m ≤ (2 \textasciicircum{} 64 -{} 1) / p}; the obligation that \texttt{u} is below \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 64}, which the C type gives, a hypothesis of the lemma that the result is \texttt{u \% p} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.barrett\_eq}); the form with the 128-bit product, which the builds of the model compile (the compiler defines \texttt{\_\_SIZEOF\_INT128\_\_}, and \texttt{RP\_NO\_INT128} is not set), for the division \texttt{u \% p} of the other builds, which gives the same remainder.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{1683}{1697}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrime?}: the prime \texttt{p} itself, for its index \texttt{pn} in the table \texttt{prime}; the table a fresh array of \texttt{p + 1} entries, for the integers that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer \texttt{int\_next} and hands back through \texttt{is\_f\_square\_p}, and the coefficients a fresh array returned with the entry, for the array \texttt{coeffs\_mod\_p} of its caller, which it fills; one loop over the residues, for the two loops of the two branches of the schedule of Horner's rule, between which \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.hornerBarrett} chooses for each residue; the residues with a square value are not counted, and the exit asks only whether one entry is true, which is the test on the count \texttt{np} and the entry \texttt{p}; the entry is made also when \texttt{f(a)} is a square for every residue and there is no point at infinity modulo \texttt{p}, where \texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, the moduli being an input of the model, and for both of its codes \texttt{1} and \texttt{2}, which only the choice of the moduli tells apart, with the density and the fields of \texttt{prec\_entry} (stage I); the entry is a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{examine\_prime} takes from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and returned, where \texttt{examine\_prime} stores it in the field \texttt{ssp} of \texttt{prec\_entry}; it keeps only \texttt{p}, the table and the inverses (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Entry}), and no rows: the table of rows of the prime, with the row of \texttt{0} from the build and the others absent (lines 1820-1821, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.primeRows}), is made in the store of the run by the loop of the tables when the prime says something (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.examinePrimes}), and for a prime that a modulus needs, one beyond the loop of the tables, which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} examines, or one that says nothing, by \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables} in the loop of \texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo} over the moduli, right after the entry; the fields \texttt{init}, \texttt{nf} and \texttt{pw} that \texttt{examine\_prime} sets (lines 1800 and 1817) and its reciprocal \texttt{magic} (line 1808) are those of the sieve entry of the prime (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry}), of which the prime is the single factor, made by \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}, which sets the reciprocal there, and so are the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of \texttt{Ratpoints.rbaLength} (lines 1815 and 1816), which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} sets there with the formulas of these lines; no density \texttt{r} (line 1811), which serves the choice of the moduli (stage I).)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2350}{2354}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}: the entry of every modulus made here, by its factors computed again from \texttt{m} (\texttt{Ratpoints.modulusFactors}), where \texttt{make\_modulus} reads the codes \texttt{fac} of the factors and their number \texttt{nf} that \texttt{add\_moduli} stores with the candidate (lines 2405-2406), and where \texttt{sieving\_info} takes the entry of a prime from the loop of the tables (\texttt{prec[n].ssp}) and makes those of the prime powers and the products by \texttt{make\_modulus}; the primes and prime powers as factors of the entry, for the fields \texttt{nf}, \texttt{pw} and \texttt{factor} and the entries of the prime powers that \texttt{make\_power} makes; the tables of a prime power (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Factor.power}) computed for each modulus that needs them, where \texttt{add\_moduli} examines a prime power once, when the factorization of the first candidate that reaches it needs it (the power itself), whether or not that candidate is then offered, and keeps its tables in its buffer \texttt{pws} by its index (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2350-2354, 2358-2359 and 2387-2394, with the count \texttt{npw} of line 2548), and \texttt{make\_modulus} makes the entry of a prime power once and keeps it by its index (\texttt{power\_se}), whose table of rows the model makes once too, for the prime power by its prime and its exponent, as the C code keeps the index of its entry in \texttt{pw\_idx[pn][e]} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef.power}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the tables of a prime power computed also when they say nothing, where \texttt{add\_moduli} refuses a modulus with such a factor (line 2395), and a prime factor whose prime says nothing (\texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, and \texttt{prime\_se[pn]} stays \texttt{NULL}) taken with its table from the loop of the tables, where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers no composite with such a factor (line 2383); a prime beyond those of the loop of the tables examined, with the exit, when the entry of a modulus needs it, where \texttt{sieving\_info} examines the primes from \texttt{prime[pn\_lim]} on, in the order of the table, with the exit, in the loop of the tables while its first two stages want more primes (lines 2693-2705; there they also give forbidden divisors) and for the third stage (lines 2976-3016), both only when the number of primes was left to the library (lines 2693 and 2980), also those that it then skips, and \texttt{add\_moduli} makes composites, prime powers and products alike, of the primes of the loop of the tables only (line 2370): the output does not depend on the primes examined, since the exit is taken only when the curve has no points; every modulus of the parameters taken, any product of powers of primes of the table below \texttt{Ratpoints.maxPrimeEven} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Params.WF}), where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers a composite only for an odd \texttt{9 ≤ m ≤ RATPOINTS\_COMPOSITE\_MAX} (line 2361; \texttt{ratpoints.h:210-{}211}, 64 by default) whose table is not too dear for the run (line 2368), a density \texttt{r < 1} (line 2402) and at most \texttt{RP\_MAX\_MODULI} candidates (line 2403), restrictions that the model lifts as choices of the moduli (stage I); the test of room in the buffer of the prime powers (lines 2351 and 2390) not made, which never fails, since \texttt{add\_moduli} runs once for the curve (line 2821, \texttt{npw = 0} at line 2548) and examines each power \texttt{p\textasciicircum{}e < RATPOINTS\_MAX\_PRIME\_EVEN} of the first \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} primes at most once (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2358-2359 and 2387-2393), all of which \texttt{num\_powers} counts; the reciprocal \texttt{magic}, the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of every kind of modulus set here, with the formulas of the C code, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets those of a prime with its table (lines 1808, 1815 and 1816), \texttt{make\_power} those of a prime power (lines 2422, 2424 and 2425) and \texttt{make\_modulus} those of a product (lines 2454, 2456 and 2457), the inverse of a prime read from its table, as from the table \texttt{inverses[pn]} of the build; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s of these formulas; the inverses \texttt{dinv} empty, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}); no density \texttt{r} (stage I); the kind \texttt{init} of the builder set here for every kind of modulus, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets that of a prime with its table (line 1800); the reference to the entry whose table of rows holds its rows (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef}), for the pointer to the entry, the position \texttt{n} of a product its own entry; the tables of rows of the entry and of its factors, which \texttt{make\_power} (line 2427) and \texttt{make\_modulus} (line 2471) clear, made in the store of the run by the loop over the moduli after the entry (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the entry a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{make\_power} and \texttt{make\_modulus} take from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime that \texttt{sieving\_info} returns.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2490}{2502}: not yet recorded (11 lines of code)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2503}{2503}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2504}{2520}: not yet recorded (16 lines of code)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2522}{2532}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}: the arguments that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the word \texttt{den\_bits} and the classes \texttt{cls}) are not modelled, nor that choice (stage I): the moduli and their stages are those of the parameters, and the primes examined in the loop of the tables their first \texttt{P.examined}, beyond which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} examines a prime when a modulus needs it; the sieve entries of every modulus made here, those of the third stage included, which \texttt{sieving\_info} puts into \texttt{sieve\_list} in the choice of the third stage (line 3014), and again, sorted by density with the reserve of \texttt{adapt\_primes}, after it (lines 3026-3030; stage I), and the reciprocals of the entries of the moduli, where \texttt{sieving\_info} collects those of the reserve too (stage I); the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} as the switch \texttt{checkDenom}, which the search clears, with the flag, when there is no forbidden divisor and no Jacobi test (\texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); the sieve entries and the forbidden divisors returned as lists and the reciprocals as an array, for the arrays \texttt{sieve\_list} and \texttt{magics} and the arrays of the arguments, with no bound \texttt{2 RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} on the number of the entries and the reciprocals (lines 332-333 and 347), which ratpoints never reaches since each of its entries owns a prime, where well-formed parameters may repeat a modulus; the store of the tables of rows returned, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries that \texttt{sieving\_info} makes; the position of a modulus the number of the entries made before it, the reference to a product (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime returned; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}, \texttt{RP\_PRIME\_STATS} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.forbidden}: the position \texttt{examined} as an argument, for the final \texttt{pn\_lim} of the loop of the tables; the Kronecker symbol by the table of the squares modulo \texttt{p}, which marks \texttt{0} as a square, for \texttt{mpz\_kronecker\_si}; the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} not tested, since the search computes the forbidden divisors only when the flag is set, for even degree (\texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}); lists, for the two arrays of the arguments with their terminating zeros; the words of one of the first \texttt{Ratpoints.numPrimes} primes an array of the first \texttt{p} words of the pattern \texttt{sieves0}, for the pointers \texttt{start} and \texttt{end} into it, and those of a prime beyond them made with its entry, for the words that \texttt{sieving\_info} makes after this loop in the buffer \texttt{forb\_words}, with no failure for lack of memory, where \texttt{sieving\_info} drops those whose words it cannot store; no reciprocals \texttt{magic}, which ratpoints reads only for the first word of a block (stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

the primes and prime powers as factors of the entry, for the fields \texttt{nf}, \texttt{pw} and \texttt{factor} and the entries of the prime powers that \texttt{make\_power} makes; the tables of a prime power (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Factor.power}) computed for each modulus that needs them, where \texttt{add\_moduli} examines a prime power once, when the factorization of the first candidate that reaches it needs it (the power itself), whether or not that candidate is then offered, and keeps its tables in its buffer \texttt{pws} by its index (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2350-2354, 2358-2359 and 2387-2394, with the count \texttt{npw} of line 2548), and \texttt{make\_modulus} makes the entry of a prime power once and keeps it by its index (\texttt{power\_se}), whose table of rows the model makes once too, for the prime power by its prime and its exponent, as the C code keeps the index of its entry in \texttt{pw\_idx[pn][e]} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef.power}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the tables of a prime power computed also when they say nothing, where \texttt{add\_moduli} refuses a modulus with such a factor (line 2395), and a prime factor whose prime says nothing (\texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, and \texttt{prime\_se[pn]} stays \texttt{NULL}) taken with its table from the loop of the tables, where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers no composite with such a factor (line 2383); a prime beyond those of the loop of the tables examined, with the exit, when the entry of a modulus needs it, where \texttt{sieving\_info} examines the primes from \texttt{prime[pn\_lim]} on, in the order of the table, with the exit, in the loop of the tables while its first two stages want more primes (lines 2693-2705; there they also give forbidden divisors) and for the third stage (lines 2976-3016), both only when the number of primes was left to the library (lines 2693 and 2980), also those that it then skips, and \texttt{add\_moduli} makes composites, prime powers and products alike, of the primes of the loop of the tables only (line 2370): the output does not depend on the primes examined, since the exit is taken only when the curve has no points; every modulus of the parameters taken, any product of powers of primes of the table below \texttt{Ratpoints.maxPrimeEven} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Params.WF}), where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers a composite only for an odd \texttt{9 ≤ m ≤ RATPOINTS\_COMPOSITE\_MAX} (line 2361; \texttt{ratpoints.h:210-{}211}, 64 by default) whose table is not too dear for the run (line 2368), a density \texttt{r < 1} (line 2402) and at most \texttt{RP\_MAX\_MODULI} candidates (line 2403), restrictions that the model lifts as choices of the moduli (stage I); the test of room in the buffer of the prime powers (lines 2351 and 2390) not made, which never fails, since \texttt{add\_moduli} runs once for the curve (line 2821, \texttt{npw = 0} at line 2548) and examines each power \texttt{p\textasciicircum{}e < RATPOINTS\_MAX\_PRIME\_EVEN} of the first \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} primes at most once (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2358-2359 and 2387-2393), all of which \texttt{num\_powers} counts; the reciprocal \texttt{magic}, the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of every kind of modulus set here, with the formulas of the C code, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets those of a prime with its table (lines 1808, 1815 and 1816), \texttt{make\_power} those of a prime power (lines 2422, 2424 and 2425) and \texttt{make\_modulus} those of a product (lines 2454, 2456 and 2457), the inverse of a prime read from its table, as from the table \texttt{inverses[pn]} of the build; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s of these formulas; the inverses \texttt{dinv} empty, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}); no density \texttt{r} (stage I); the kind \texttt{init} of the builder set here for every kind of modulus, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets that of a prime with its table (line 1800); the reference to the entry whose table of rows holds its rows (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef}), for the pointer to the entry, the position \texttt{n} of a product its own entry; the tables of rows of the entry and of its factors, which \texttt{make\_power} (line 2427) and \texttt{make\_modulus} (line 2471) clear, made in the store of the run by the loop over the moduli after the entry (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the entry a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{make\_power} and \texttt{make\_modulus} take from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime that \texttt{sieving\_info} returns.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2561}{2562}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.forbidden}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.forbidden}: the position \texttt{examined} as an argument, for the final \texttt{pn\_lim} of the loop of the tables; the Kronecker symbol by the table of the squares modulo \texttt{p}, which marks \texttt{0} as a square, for \texttt{mpz\_kronecker\_si}; the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} not tested, since the search computes the forbidden divisors only when the flag is set, for even degree (\texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}); lists, for the two arrays of the arguments with their terminating zeros; the words of one of the first \texttt{Ratpoints.numPrimes} primes an array of the first \texttt{p} words of the pattern \texttt{sieves0}, for the pointers \texttt{start} and \texttt{end} into it, and those of a prime beyond them made with its entry, for the words that \texttt{sieving\_info} makes after this loop in the buffer \texttt{forb\_words}, with no failure for lack of memory, where \texttt{sieving\_info} drops those whose words it cannot store; no reciprocals \texttt{magic}, which ratpoints reads only for the first word of a block (stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s; no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2566}{2566}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2693}{2705}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2793}{2795}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments, and the sieve entries as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list} that \texttt{sieving\_info} fills and \texttt{class\_offsets} reads; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the store of the tables of rows that \texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo} returns handed to the sieving as a value, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries of \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list}; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits return the delivery as it came, with nothing delivered, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the count \texttt{0}; the delivery passed and returned, for the pointer \texttt{info}, the local flag \texttt{quit} of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} and the count \texttt{total}, and the result with the bits of the flags written back (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), for the bits that \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} sets in \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the sieving always follows the points at infinity unless the callback has stopped the search, so that under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} the model delivers the numerators that pass the sieve where the C code, its search region empty, delivers only the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2801}{2801}: excluded (memory): the enlargement of ba\_buffer for the primes that the loop of the tables of sieving\_info looked at beyond num\_primes, which fails only for lack of memory
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2808}{2808}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2892}{2900}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}: the arguments that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the word \texttt{den\_bits} and the classes \texttt{cls}) are not modelled, nor that choice (stage I): the moduli and their stages are those of the parameters, and the primes examined in the loop of the tables their first \texttt{P.examined}, beyond which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} examines a prime when a modulus needs it; the sieve entries of every modulus made here, those of the third stage included, which \texttt{sieving\_info} puts into \texttt{sieve\_list} in the choice of the third stage (line 3014), and again, sorted by density with the reserve of \texttt{adapt\_primes}, after it (lines 3026-3030; stage I), and the reciprocals of the entries of the moduli, where \texttt{sieving\_info} collects those of the reserve too (stage I); the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} as the switch \texttt{checkDenom}, which the search clears, with the flag, when there is no forbidden divisor and no Jacobi test (\texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); the sieve entries and the forbidden divisors returned as lists and the reciprocals as an array, for the arrays \texttt{sieve\_list} and \texttt{magics} and the arrays of the arguments, with no bound \texttt{2 RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} on the number of the entries and the reciprocals (lines 332-333 and 347), which ratpoints never reaches since each of its entries owns a prime, where well-formed parameters may repeat a modulus; the store of the tables of rows returned, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries that \texttt{sieving\_info} makes; the position of a modulus the number of the entries made before it, the reference to a product (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime returned; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}, \texttt{RP\_PRIME\_STATS} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{2922}{2922}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{2976}{2978}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}: the entry of every modulus made here, by its factors computed again from \texttt{m} (\texttt{Ratpoints.modulusFactors}), where \texttt{make\_modulus} reads the codes \texttt{fac} of the factors and their number \texttt{nf} that \texttt{add\_moduli} stores with the candidate (lines 2405-2406), and where \texttt{sieving\_info} takes the entry of a prime from the loop of the tables (\texttt{prec[n].ssp}) and makes those of the prime powers and the products by \texttt{make\_modulus}; the primes and prime powers as factors of the entry, for the fields \texttt{nf}, \texttt{pw} and \texttt{factor} and the entries of the prime powers that \texttt{make\_power} makes; the tables of a prime power (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.Factor.power}) computed for each modulus that needs them, where \texttt{add\_moduli} examines a prime power once, when the factorization of the first candidate that reaches it needs it (the power itself), whether or not that candidate is then offered, and keeps its tables in its buffer \texttt{pws} by its index (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2350-2354, 2358-2359 and 2387-2394, with the count \texttt{npw} of line 2548), and \texttt{make\_modulus} makes the entry of a prime power once and keeps it by its index (\texttt{power\_se}), whose table of rows the model makes once too, for the prime power by its prime and its exponent, as the C code keeps the index of its entry in \texttt{pw\_idx[pn][e]} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef.power}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the tables of a prime power computed also when they say nothing, where \texttt{add\_moduli} refuses a modulus with such a factor (line 2395), and a prime factor whose prime says nothing (\texttt{examine\_prime} returns \texttt{0}, and \texttt{prime\_se[pn]} stays \texttt{NULL}) taken with its table from the loop of the tables, where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers no composite with such a factor (line 2383); a prime beyond those of the loop of the tables examined, with the exit, when the entry of a modulus needs it, where \texttt{sieving\_info} examines the primes from \texttt{prime[pn\_lim]} on, in the order of the table, with the exit, in the loop of the tables while its first two stages want more primes (lines 2693-2705; there they also give forbidden divisors) and for the third stage (lines 2976-3016), both only when the number of primes was left to the library (lines 2693 and 2980), also those that it then skips, and \texttt{add\_moduli} makes composites, prime powers and products alike, of the primes of the loop of the tables only (line 2370): the output does not depend on the primes examined, since the exit is taken only when the curve has no points; every modulus of the parameters taken, any product of powers of primes of the table below \texttt{Ratpoints.maxPrimeEven} (\texttt{Ratpoints.Params.WF}), where \texttt{add\_moduli} offers a composite only for an odd \texttt{9 ≤ m ≤ RATPOINTS\_COMPOSITE\_MAX} (line 2361; \texttt{ratpoints.h:210-{}211}, 64 by default) whose table is not too dear for the run (line 2368), a density \texttt{r < 1} (line 2402) and at most \texttt{RP\_MAX\_MODULI} candidates (line 2403), restrictions that the model lifts as choices of the moduli (stage I); the test of room in the buffer of the prime powers (lines 2351 and 2390) not made, which never fails, since \texttt{add\_moduli} runs once for the curve (line 2821, \texttt{npw = 0} at line 2548) and examines each power \texttt{p\textasciicircum{}e < RATPOINTS\_MAX\_PRIME\_EVEN} of the first \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} primes at most once (\texttt{pw\_idx}, lines 2358-2359 and 2387-2393), all of which \texttt{num\_powers} counts; the reciprocal \texttt{magic}, the bias \texttt{bias} and the inverse \texttt{rbainv} of every kind of modulus set here, with the formulas of the C code, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets those of a prime with its table (lines 1808, 1815 and 1816), \texttt{make\_power} those of a prime power (lines 2422, 2424 and 2425) and \texttt{make\_modulus} those of a product (lines 2454, 2456 and 2457), the inverse of a prime read from its table, as from the table \texttt{inverses[pn]} of the build; natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s of these formulas; the inverses \texttt{dinv} empty, which the row offsets of the packing fill (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.classOffsets}); no density \texttt{r} (stage I); the kind \texttt{init} of the builder set here for every kind of modulus, where \texttt{examine\_prime} sets that of a prime with its table (line 1800); the reference to the entry whose table of rows holds its rows (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.EntryRef}), for the pointer to the entry, the position \texttt{n} of a product its own entry; the tables of rows of the entry and of its factors, which \texttt{make\_power} (line 2427) and \texttt{make\_modulus} (line 2471) clear, made in the store of the run by the loop over the moduli after the entry (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.SieveEntry.addTables}); the entry a fresh value, for the space that \texttt{make\_power} and \texttt{make\_modulus} take from the buffer of the sieve entries (\texttt{se\_next}), and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime that \texttt{sieving\_info} returns.)

stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); \item \csource{find_points.c}{3064}{3070}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sievingInfo}: the arguments that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the word \texttt{den\_bits} and the classes \texttt{cls}) are not modelled, nor that choice (stage I): the moduli and their stages are those of the parameters, and the primes examined in the loop of the tables their first \texttt{P.examined}, beyond which \texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?} examines a prime when a modulus needs it; the sieve entries of every modulus made here, those of the third stage included, which \texttt{sieving\_info} puts into \texttt{sieve\_list} in the choice of the third stage (line 3014), and again, sorted by density with the reserve of \texttt{adapt\_primes}, after it (lines 3026-3030; stage I), and the reciprocals of the entries of the moduli, where \texttt{sieving\_info} collects those of the reserve too (stage I); the flag \texttt{RATPOINTS\_CHECK\_DENOM} as the switch \texttt{checkDenom}, which the search clears, with the flag, when there is no forbidden divisor and no Jacobi test (\texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); the sieve entries and the forbidden divisors returned as lists and the reciprocals as an array, for the arrays \texttt{sieve\_list} and \texttt{magics} and the arrays of the arguments, with no bound \texttt{2 RATPOINTS\_NUM\_PRIMES} on the number of the entries and the reciprocals (lines 332-333 and 347), which ratpoints never reaches since each of its entries owns a prime, where well-formed parameters may repeat a modulus; the store of the tables of rows returned, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries that \texttt{sieving\_info} makes; the position of a modulus the number of the entries made before it, the reference to a product (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); and the exit as \texttt{none}, for the prime returned; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}, \texttt{RP\_PRIME\_STATS} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{3112}{3114}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}: every numerator from \texttt{-{}H} to \texttt{H}, for the intervals of the search region that the Sturm step keeps (stage H), returning at the first interval beyond \texttt{H} and skipping an empty one, whose ends \texttt{interval\_bits} computes and clips to the height bound (lines 3426-3427), with the form of \texttt{numerators\_to\_bits} that the whole line takes: the plain one, which \texttt{interval\_bits} takes (line 3432), when \texttt{exact\_bounds} finds the forms of the ends of an interval, for \texttt{H ≤ LONG\_MAX -{} 64} (lines 3332-3338), and otherwise the split one, which \texttt{interval\_bits\_exact} takes (line 3404) (stage H); the height bound converted to \texttt{Int64}, which is exact for \texttt{H < 2 \textasciicircum{} 63}, and the bits back to integers; the sieve specs, and with them the rows of the residues, made before the bits of the interval, where \texttt{sift} turns the interval into bits first and makes them (the flag \texttt{do\_setup}) once \texttt{interval\_bits} does not report an interval empty (it returns 0 also for an interval that holds no numerator, lines 3426-3427), which for the whole line is at once, and so before the test \texttt{low ≤ high} of the bits (line 3568); one call of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.setRows}, for the two calls with the flag \texttt{shared} a constant, between which the pool of threads chooses (stage I); the store of the tables of rows passed and returned, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries of the arguments, which \texttt{sift} reaches through \texttt{sieve\_list} and which keep the rows built for the rest of the run; the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, the entries \texttt{es} and the reciprocals \texttt{mgs} of the first two stages, the entries \texttt{es3} of the third stage and their reciprocals \texttt{mgs3} as arguments, for the numbers \texttt{sp1}, \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} that the sieving thread keeps (\texttt{worker\_init}), the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[0], …, sieve\_list[sp2 -{} 1]}, the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} reads, and the entries \texttt{sieve\_list[sp2], …, sieve\_list[sp3 -{} 1]} and the reciprocals \texttt{magics[sp2], …, magics[sp3 -{} 1]}, which \texttt{fill\_checks} reads, with no correction of \texttt{sp2} and \texttt{sp3} between the blocks of the run (stage I); the residues \texttt{bp} and the class \texttt{cl} as values, for the pointers \texttt{bp\_list} and \texttt{cls}, and the array \texttt{offsets} of the row offsets of the run as an argument, which the C code reaches through the pointer \texttt{offset} of the class; the thunk of \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.fillChecks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{fill\_checks} fills, and its flag \texttt{stage3\_filled}, which \texttt{sift} clears; the thunk of the products \texttt{w}, for the flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; no count of the denominators sieved (\texttt{n\_sifts}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit}, which \texttt{worker\_init} clears, and the count \texttt{total} that \texttt{sift} keeps from zero and returns; the arguments of the run passed explicitly, for the pointer \texttt{args} of the sieving thread (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}), which \texttt{worker\_init} sets and through which \texttt{sift} reads them; no search intervals \texttt{iv} of the sieving thread (\texttt{rp-{}private.h:574}), which \texttt{worker\_init} clears (\texttt{find\_points.c:3130}) and \texttt{run\_block} sets for each block (\texttt{find\_points.c:3913}; stage H); no pool, slot and stop flag of a thread of the pool, the flag by which the pool of threads tells it to abandon its block (\texttt{pool}, \texttt{slot}, \texttt{stop}, \texttt{rp-{}private.h:584-{}585}; stage I); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_SIFT\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_SETUP\_TIC} and their \texttt{TOC}) and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4082}{4519}: not yet recorded (307 lines of code)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4523}{4528}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsWith}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsWith}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), returned apart from the outcome, for the negative codes of the library (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NON\_SQUAREFREE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_BAD\_ARGS}; \texttt{RATPOINTS\_WORK\_LENGTH\_TOO\_SMALL} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY} cannot arise), which share the \texttt{long} that \texttt{find\_points} returns with the count: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count and three bits of the flags (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region, and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it (where the C code returns at line 4889, for even degree only, with the bits \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES1} clear, as the model writes them back), is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set and under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} the model delivers the survivors of all numerators \texttt{-{}H, …, H}: the C code delivers only those in the intervals that the Sturm step keeps, none when the region misses \texttt{[-{}H, H]} (\texttt{sturm\_empty}, only the points at infinity), and nothing at all when the form is negative everywhere (line 4889, even degree, no point at infinity). No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4542}{4545}: excluded (interface): the input fields of the arguments that find\_points\_work saves, so that a caller who reuses the arguments for the next curve does not find the normalizations and choices of the search in them; the model writes nothing back

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4577}{4577}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count and three bits of the flags (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region, and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it (where the C code returns at line 4889, for even degree only, with the bits \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES1} clear, as the model writes them back), is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set and under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} the model delivers the survivors of all numerators \texttt{-{}H, …, H}: the C code delivers only those in the intervals that the Sturm step keeps, none when the region misses \texttt{[-{}H, H]} (\texttt{sturm\_empty}, only the points at infinity), and nothing at all when the form is negative everywhere (line 4889, even degree, no point at infinity). No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)
\item \csource{find_points.c}{4607}{4607}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.searchPoints}: the arguments of \texttt{sieving\_info} that serve the choice of the moduli (the mean number of bits per word, whether the number of primes was left to the library, the 2-adic classes and the word \texttt{den\_bits}) are not modelled; the denominators from \texttt{1} to \texttt{H}, for the range \texttt{b\_low, …, b\_high} (stage H); the flags of the denominators as Booleans, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the forbidden divisors and the divisors of the leading coefficient with their records as lists, for the arrays \texttt{args-{}>forb\_ba}, \texttt{args-{}>forbidden}, \texttt{args-{}>den\_info} and \texttt{args-{}>divisors} of the arguments, and the sieve entries as a list, for the array \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list} that \texttt{sieving\_info} fills and \texttt{class\_offsets} reads; the square test \texttt{lcfsq} of line 4906 made on the polynomial searched (\texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.isSquare}), where the C code computes it before the reversal check (line 4634) and clears it in case 2 (line 4770): the same value for an even degree, the only one that reads it; the store of the tables of rows that \texttt{Ratpoints.sievingInfo} returns handed to the sieving as a value, for the arrays \texttt{sieve} of the entries of \texttt{args-{}>sieve\_list}; the test on \texttt{point\_at\_infty} of the 2-adic exit recomputed, as \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity} decides it; the exits return the delivery as it came, with nothing delivered, where \texttt{sieving\_info} returns the prime and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} the count \texttt{0}; the delivery passed and returned, for the pointer \texttt{info}, the local flag \texttt{quit} of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} and the count \texttt{total}, and the result with the bits of the flags written back (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), for the bits that \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1} sets in \texttt{args-{}>flags}; the Sturm step does not restrict the search region before stage H, so that the return when it leaves nothing to search is never taken, and the sieving always follows the points at infinity unless the callback has stopped the search, so that under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} the model delivers the numerators that pass the sieve where the C code, its search region empty, delivers only the points at infinity; no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}.)

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}: the flags \texttt{fl} as an argument, for the bits \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED}, \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} of the flags of the search (\texttt{args-{}>flags}); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointer \texttt{info}, the local flag \texttt{quit} and the count \texttt{total} of \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}; the return when the callback stops the search (lines 5100-5103) made by the caller (\texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}); no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE} or \texttt{DEBUG}; the square test of \texttt{c\_d} and the decision whether there are points at infinity are made on the list that it is given, after the reversal check, when the points are delivered, where the C code computes \texttt{lcfsq} before the check (line 4634), which clears it in case 2 (line 4770), the only reversal after which the degree is even, and leaves it, unread, with the odd degree that cases 1 and 3 leave, and sets \texttt{point\_at\_infty} before the exits of the search (lines 4894-4899); the square root by \texttt{Nat.sqrt}, for \texttt{mpz\_sqrt}.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{4643}{4649}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.sieveParams}: the moduli are the first primes of the table, in increasing order, where ratpoints ranks the primes by what they say about the curve and adds composite moduli (\texttt{sieving\_info}; stage I), and takes the entries of its stages from that ranking, skipping a modulus that shares a prime with one taken (\texttt{take\_entries}); it leaves the primes that say nothing out of its pool (lines 1764-1765 and 2613-2622), and those that say only that the numerator is prime to the denominator stay in the pool of the first two stages without counting toward the primes that it looks for (\texttt{n\_weak}, line 2704) and leave the pool of the third stage with the composite moduli not taken (lines 2873-2890 and 2999-3000); so the counts that the options fix, of the first stage under \texttt{-{}n}, of the first two stages under \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}N} (or \texttt{-{}n} and \texttt{-{}U 0} without \texttt{-{}R}) and of all the moduli under \texttt{-{}n}, \texttt{-{}N} and \texttt{-{}P}, bound those of ratpoints, which can be smaller, while where an option is absent ratpoints can take more moduli in a stage or fewer (no bound on a stage for \texttt{-{}N} without \texttt{-{}n}, nor for \texttt{-{}P} alone); without \texttt{-{}n}, the first stage ends at \texttt{Ratpoints.defaultSp1}, the fixed choice of the header, where ratpoints chooses the end from the curve by its costs (stage I); without \texttt{-{}N}, the second stage adds the flat offset \texttt{Ratpoints.sp2Extra}, as ratpoints does under \texttt{-{}U 0} (\texttt{phase\_2\_offset} for \texttt{u0 = 0}), where it otherwise scales the offset by the length of the run (stage I), and the model ignores \texttt{-{}R}, whose value ratpoints takes in place of \texttt{RATPOINTS\_SP2\_EXTRA} (lines 2571-2572 and 2808) and which comes with the scaled offset (stage I); without \texttt{-{}P}, the third stage is the rest of the first \texttt{q} primes, where ratpoints takes the primes of its pool in increasing order of their density \texttt{r}, the most selective first, stops by its cost rule (lines 2949-2992; stage I) and may look past the first \texttt{q} when \texttt{-{}p} is absent; the primes examined are the first \texttt{q}, where ratpoints, when \texttt{-{}p} is absent, looks at further primes while its pool is short of the moduli that its first two stages want, and later for its third stage, \texttt{-{}p} being a hard limit of the first two stages (line 2693) as of the third (line 2980), and the model examines the primes of its moduli beyond the first \texttt{q} when it makes their entries (\texttt{Ratpoints.makeModulus?}); no correction of the moduli during the run (\texttt{adapt\_primes}, stage I); natural numbers for the \texttt{long}s, so that the sums of the counts cannot overflow.)

\item \csource{find_points.c}{5215}{5217}: excluded (instrumentation): the message under DEBUG at the end of find\_points\_work\_1
\item \csource{find_points.c}{5219}{5220}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsWith}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.findPointsWith}: one function for \texttt{find\_points}, \texttt{find\_points\_work} and \texttt{find\_points\_work\_1}, which the library calls in turn. The refusals of the program, in its order and with its errors (\texttt{Ratpoints.Refusal}), returned apart from the outcome, for the negative codes of the library (\texttt{RATPOINTS\_NON\_SQUAREFREE} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_BAD\_ARGS}; \texttt{RATPOINTS\_WORK\_LENGTH\_TOO\_SMALL} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_MEMORY} cannot arise), which share the \texttt{long} that \texttt{find\_points} returns with the count: fewer than two coefficients are refused on the length of \texttt{c}, as the program refuses them, where the library refuses an empty list as a negative degree and one coefficient as the degree 0 (a longer list of degree 0 fails the test of the leading zeros first); and the height bound, which the program checks before it calls the library, comes before the test of the leading zeros, which the library makes first, so that \texttt{5 0} with \texttt{H = 0} is error 4, as the program gives it. The degree with the leading zeros dropped is \texttt{Ratpoints.BruteForce.degree c}. A natural number \texttt{H} for the \texttt{long} \texttt{height} of the arguments (\texttt{ratpoints.h:362}), so that \texttt{H = 0} stands for the heights below 1 that line 4658 refuses; a height that is not a \texttt{long}, \texttt{2 \textasciicircum{} 63} or more, is refused with error 4, as the program refuses it when it reads the height (\texttt{Ratpoints.Cli.heightBound}), where the library cannot be given one, its height being a \texttt{long}. A list for the array of GMP integers and its scratch integers \texttt{work}, with nothing written back to the caller but the data of the callback, the count and three bits of the flags (\texttt{Ratpoints.Outcome}), so that there is no state between calls and the reset of the flags clears nothing; the callback a function that returns what the call gives (\texttt{Ratpoints.Answer}), and its data a value, for the pointer \texttt{info}; the options of the output as fields of the options (\texttt{Ratpoints.Options}), copied into the flags of the check (\texttt{Ratpoints.CheckFlags}) with the flag of the reversal, for the bits of \texttt{args-{}>flags} that the mask of line 4606 keeps; the points at infinity and the square test of the leading coefficient are decided where they are used (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.pointsAtInfinity}, \texttt{Ratpoints.Setup.reversal}, \texttt{Ratpoints.searchPoints}). Of the Sturm step only its test for a repeated factor: the rest, which restricts the search region, and its exit when the polynomial is negative on the whole of it (where the C code returns at line 4889, for even degree only, with the bits \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_USE\_SQUARES1} clear, as the model writes them back), is stage H, so that \texttt{sturm\_empty} is never set and under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} the model delivers the survivors of all numerators \texttt{-{}H, …, H}: the C code delivers only those in the intervals that the Sturm step keeps, none when the region misses \texttt{[-{}H, H]} (\texttt{sturm\_empty}, only the points at infinity), and nothing at all when the form is negative everywhere (line 4889, even degree, no point at infinity). No search region (stage H); no failure for lack of memory, which the model cannot meet; no output under \texttt{RATPOINTS\_VERBOSE}.)

\begin{itemize}

\item \csource{sift.c}{194}{201}: excluded (instrumentation): RP\_STOP\_AFTER, development instrumentation that cuts the pipeline short after a step so that its cost can be measured, 0 in the production build, with the exact check of its level 4 replaced by a count

  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.checkPoint}: the products \texttt{w} as a thunk, which the sieve of one denominator makes for each denominator (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sift}) and which is forced when the first numerator of \texttt{b} reaches the check, for the array \texttt{work} of the sieving thread, which \texttt{worker\_init} gives it, and its flag \texttt{compute\_bc}, which \texttt{sift} sets and \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} clears when it computes the products; the degree \texttt{d} and the flags \texttt{fl} as arguments, handed down from \texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.sieveRun} through the components that call the check, for the degree and the bits \texttt{RATPOINTS\_REVERSED}, \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_CHECK} and \texttt{RATPOINTS\_NO\_Y} of the flags of the search, which \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} reads through its worker (\texttt{args-{}>degree}, \texttt{args-{}>flags}); the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} keeps from zero and returns, and the three branches of the map of the reversal at each call one definition (\texttt{Ratpoints.Delivery.callMapped}); the square root and the test of the remainder by \texttt{Nat.sqrt} on \texttt{v}, for \texttt{mpz\_sqrtrem}; integers for the \texttt{long}s \texttt{a} and \texttt{b} (the negations of the map stay \texttt{long}s by \texttt{Ratpoints.fitsLong\_neg}); no measurements of the time of the check and of its products (\texttt{RP\_CHECK}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_BC\_TOC} under \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}), and no output under \texttt{DEBUG}.)
\item \csource{sift.c}{207}{213}: excluded (instrumentation): the sink into which the levels of RP\_STOP\_AFTER accumulate the work they leave out, printed on stderr at exit

\item \csource{sift.c}{262}{264}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.walkWord}

\item \csource{sift.c}{318}{327}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.relprime}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.relprime}: \texttt{Int64} for \texttt{long}, \texttt{toUInt64} for the cast to \texttt{unsigned long}, and the \texttt{toInt64} of the count for the \texttt{long} that \texttt{RP\_CTZL} returns; the negation of a negative \texttt{m} as a conditional expression, for the statement \texttt{if(m < 0)}; for \texttt{m = -{}2 \textasciicircum{} 63}, whose negation overflows in the C code, the model wraps; the contract excludes that value, which the search never passes, its numerators being at most \texttt{H < 2 \textasciicircum{} 63} in absolute value; \texttt{m \&\&\& 1 == 0} for \texttt{!(m \& 1)}; the lowest set bit by the loop of \texttt{RP\_CTZL} for a compiler without the builtin (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.ctz}), where gcc and clang take \texttt{\_\_builtin\_ctzl}; the builtin is undefined on \texttt{0} and the loop does not end there, which the contract excludes, with \texttt{n ≥ 1} and \texttt{m ≠ 0} at the calls; the loop of the binary algorithm a function of its own (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.relprimeOdd}); a Boolean for the \texttt{int}.)
\item \csource{sift.c}{328}{342}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.relprimeOdd}

the thunk \texttt{w} of the products of the check as an argument, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it; the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} keeps from zero and returns, and its returns at a stop within the walk through the set bits of a word passed on by the scan (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}); \item \csource{sift.c}{1300}{1305}: modelled by \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftPiece}
  (deviation of \lname{Ratpoints.Sieve.siftPiece}: the arm of the first stage chosen by a test on the constant \texttt{Ratpoints.chunk}, for the conditional compilation \texttt{\#if (RATPOINTS\_CHUNK > 1) \&\& (RATPOINTS\_CHUNK <= 16)} (\texttt{sift.c:452}, \texttt{sift.c:575}, \texttt{sift.c:943}), which compiles one arm only, and \texttt{tail\_leg} with the chunked one; a fresh array of zeros for each piece, for the survivors array of the sieving thread, which every piece reuses, with one bit array more for the alignment, and whose words \texttt{malloc} leaves uninitialized; the piece by its first word number \texttt{w0} and its number \texttt{n} of bit arrays, for \texttt{w\_low} and \texttt{w\_high}, and an index for the pointer to its last bit array; the moduli of the first two stages with their rows and offsets as the list \texttt{specs} and the end \texttt{sp1} of the first stage, for the sieve specs \texttt{sieves} and the number \texttt{sp1} that the sieving thread keeps, the reciprocals of their moduli as the list \texttt{mgs}, for the array \texttt{magics} of the arguments, and the thunk \texttt{checks}, for the table \texttt{checks} of the third stage and its length \texttt{nchecks = sp3 -{} sp2}; the class \texttt{cl} as a value, for the pointer \texttt{cls}; integers for the \texttt{long}s of the test \texttt{small}, which stay \texttt{long}s, and a Boolean for its \texttt{int}; no count of the words of the piece (\texttt{n\_words}), which ratpoints reads to correct the moduli between the blocks of the run (stage I); the thunk \texttt{w} of the products of the check as an argument, where \texttt{\_ratpoints\_check\_point} computes the products when the first survivor of \texttt{b} reaches it; the delivery \texttt{r} passed and returned, for the pointers \texttt{info} and \texttt{wk-{}>quit} and the count \texttt{total} that \texttt{\_ratpoints\_sift0} keeps from zero and returns, and its returns at a stop within the walk through the set bits of a word passed on by the scan (\texttt{Ratpoints.Sieve.scanPiece}); natural numbers and integers for the \texttt{long}s; no measurements of the phases (\texttt{RP\_TIC}, \texttt{RP\_TOC}, \texttt{RP\_PHASE\_TIMING}) and no stop after one of them (\texttt{RP\_STOP\_AFTER}).)

\item \csource{sturm.c}{166}{332}: not yet recorded (136 lines of code)
